top.title: 2027: INEC condemns ‘rig and die’ slogan, vows sanctions for electoral offenders
top.description: . Seeks media partnership to safeguard democracy . Warns against fake results, inflammatory rhetoric By Steve Oko & Chinedu Adonu The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has condemned the “rig and die” slogan being popularised by some political actors ahead of the 2027 general elections, warning that it could expose innocent Nigerians to electoral violence. The Commission also vowed that any electoral official, including ad hoc personnel, found to have compromised the electoral process would face the full weight of the law. INEC National Commissioner and Chairman, Information and Voter Education Committee, Mohammed Kudu Haruna, gave the warnings at a media engagement forum for journalists and media executives from the South-East, South-South and South-West geopolitical zones in Enugu. Haruna cautioned politicians against inflammatory rhetoric and threats capable of endangering ordinary Nigerians engaged as presiding officers, ad hoc staff, party agents and election observers. He stressed that disagreements over electoral outcomes should be resolved through lawful channels, including complaints to INEC, security agencies and the courts, rather than violence. The National Commissioner also sought stronger collaboration with the media to safeguard democracy and ensure credible, peaceful and transparent conduct of the 2027 elections. Describing the media as critical to electoral credibility, he said public confidence in the electoral process depended largely on the accuracy, fairness and professionalism of election reporting. He cautioned journalists against spreading misinformation, unverified results, manipulated videos and inflammatory political narratives capable of undermining public confidence and triggering violence. Haruna particularly warned against premature declaration of results, sensational reporting and presenting projections as official results. “Results are declared only by the Commission through its duly appointed returning officers. Projections and unofficial figures must be clearly labelled as such,” he said. He urged journalists to verify allegations against INEC through its official channels before publication and report electoral incidents with sensitivity, distinguishing between events personally witnessed and information obtained from other sources. The National Commissioner further called for inclusive election reporting that gives adequate attention to women, youths and persons with disabilities, particularly the challenges they face in participating in the electoral process. He urged media organisations to intensify voter education, especially on Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs), accreditation procedures, electronic transmission of results and peaceful participation. top.title: CHOGM 2026: Bianca seeks stronger commonwealth cooperation
top.description: Nigeria has called for stronger cooperation among Commonwealth member states to address security challenges, expand trade, strengthen democratic institutions and promote climate resilience. The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu, disclosed this on Monday in a post on her X account, detailing Nigeria’s expectations from the Commonwealth following her interventions at the 2026 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) in Antigua. She said Nigeria emphasised the need for collective action on peace and security, trade, climate resilience and youth empowerment, particularly in combating terrorism and expanding access to development finance. Odumegwu-Ojukwu also drew attention to Nigeria’s preparations for the 2027 general elections, stressing the importance of supporting free, fair and credible electoral processes through election monitoring groups and stronger democratic institutions across member states. According to her, Nigeria, under President Bola Tinubu’s leadership, remains committed to promoting democracy, consensus, civil, political and social rights, while upholding the rule of law and judicial independence. She described the creation of the Commonwealth Trade Portal as a welcome development, noting that trade facilitation initiatives would promote economic growth, strengthen trade links among member states and help developing economies integrate into the global financial market. The minister further urged the Commonwealth to give greater attention to women and girls affected by conflicts, displacement and climate change. She said their access to essential services, livelihood opportunities and justice should remain central to collective responses, adding that their voices must shape solutions to the challenges they face. On reparatory justice, Odumegwu-Ojukwu identified the agenda as a major highlight of the ministerial meeting, particularly the agreement by the United Kingdom government to engage in structured, time-bound, inclusive and good-faith dialogue with affected countries over the transatlantic trafficking of enslaved Africans and its historical consequences. She said Nigeria hoped that the commitments adopted at CHOGM 2026 would translate into practical actions capable of creating jobs, strengthening security and improving the lives of citizens across Commonwealth member states. top.title: Tim Parker Hangs Up Cleats After Final Match For New York
top.description: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images Tim Parker played his last professional game on Saturday, November 7, 2026. The 33-year-old defender stepped onto the field at Sports Illustrated Stadium in Harrison, New Jersey, for one final match. He came on in the 90th minute to replace Sekou Kone during a 3-0 victory over Atlanta United. The crowd watched a local boy finish his career with a win, playing into the third minute of stoppage time before the final whistle blew. This was not just a game; it was the end of a 12-year journey through Major League Soccer. Parker, a native of Hicksville, New York, played 304 league matches in total. He chose to leave the sport on his own terms after a decade of hard work. The Red Bull New York team honored him by handing him the captain’s armband for this farewell performance. A Career Built on Hard Work Parker’s path to the top was not easy. He spent five years with Vancouver, making 100 appearances and scoring four goals. In 2015, he helped his team win the Canadian Championship. His time in Houston came next, where he played for two seasons and served as co-captain for both 2021 and 2022. He also spent two seasons with St. Louis CITY SC, scoring six goals there, including the very first goal in the club’s history. His most successful stretch came with the Red Bulls, where he played five seasons and made 128 appearances across all competitions. This number is higher than his time with any other club. In his first year with New York in 2018, he helped the team win the Supporters Shield. That same year, the club set a record for the most points in a single MLS season. The defense Parker anchored allowed only 33 goals, which was the fewest in the league. They also kept 15 clean sheets, the highest total in the league that year. He said, “Tim’s career speaks for itself.” The coach emphasized that Parker gave every team he joined leadership, presence, and quality. Bradley explained that the way Parker treated his teammates made him a proud figure in the dressing room. Julian de Guzman, the Head of Sport for Red Bull New York, also praised the retiring defender. According to reports, he has maintained an outstanding professional status throughout his career. De Guzman noted that Parker earned the respect of everyone he played with and worked alongside. At every club he represented, Parker’s leadership, professionalism, commitment, and passion made him an important figure, he highlighted. The official statement from the club confirmed that Parker’s impact extends well beyond what he accomplished on the field. top.title: Jaguars reportedly acquiring Falcons' Pro Bowl safety in major trade
top.description: Jaguars reportedly acquiring Falcons' Pro Bowl safety in major trade originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Jacksonville Jaguars beat the Baltimore Ravens in Week 9 and were clear buyers for the 2026 NFL trade deadline. Sitting comfortably atop the AFC South, the Jaguars needed some help. Looking at this roster, two main needs came into focus: defensive tackle and safety. While they've yet to make a move in the DT market, the Jaguars have reportedly made their safety move, and it's a massive one. According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , the Jaguars are sending the Atlanta Falcons two draft picks to acquire Pro Bowl safety Jessie Bates, one of the best safeties in the NFL, to get a major upgrade on the defensive side of the ball. Jaguars to acquire Jessie Bates from Falcons for two picks "Trade: Falcons are sending former Pro Bowl safety Jessie Bates to the Jacksonville Jaguars in exchange for a 2027 2nd-round pick and a 2028 5th-round pick, sources tell ESPN," Schefter reports. This is a massive move for the Jaguars prior to the Tuesday trade deadline, as Bates is one of the best defensive backs in the NFL and was one of the more intriguing trade candidates seemingly available this season. He's a 29-year-old safety who was a Pro Bowler one time back in 2023. While he might not have a lot of accolades, Bates is an incredible DB who will be a major upgrade in Jacksonville. MORE : 4 stats that show how bad Chargers' Justin Herbert has been in 2026 In his nine-year NFL career, Bates has 28 interceptions, four pick-sixes, 74 passes defended, 14 forced fumbles, 871 tackles, and one sack. This season for the Falcons, Bates has 60 total tackles with one fumble returned for a touchdown, three forced fumbles, one interception, and three passes defended. There might not have been a better safety on the trade block this season than Bates, and James Gladstone is swinging big with this major acquisition. It's a big trade, as the Jaguars giving up a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick isn't a cheap package to give up for a rental DB. But with a real chance of winning the Super Bowl, the Jaguars are going all in. top.title: Friedel group completes Shrewsbury Town takeover
top.description: Roland Wycherley has been Shrewsbury Town owner and chairman since 1996 [Shrewsbury Town FC] Shrewsbury Town's long-drawn-out takeover deal has been completed, allowing former USA international goalkeeper Brad Friedel to come in as the Shropshire outfit's new sporting director. The paperwork on the share purchase agreement with Scott Davidson's American-based consortium Biscayne ST LLC - which includes Friedel - has been finalised, taking up 87.4 per cent of the League Two club's shares and allowing long-time owner Roland Wycherley to finally let go. Miami-based businessman Davidson is joined on the new Town board by New York financier Will Dotson and Craig Graham, chairman of Spartans, the Edinburgh-based Scottish League Two club, while former Liverpool, Blackburn Rovers, Aston Villa and Tottenham Hotspur keeper Friedel will come in to take a hands-on role, working with manager Gavin Cowan. Davidson becomes chairman of the board, which still includes existing members Liam Dooley, the club's chief executive, and Duncan Montgomery, while another ex-goalkeeper, Bryan Finnerty, is to join the group, pending the EFL's owners and directors' tests. After 30 years of leading the Shropshire club, since succeeding Ray Bailey as chairman in the summer of 1996, Wycherley can now retire at the age of 85. The Shrewsbury-born lifelong fan first made his intention clear to sell more than five years ago when the Town were still a League One club. But his dogged determination to do a deal he had to be convinced was right for the club's long-term future before he handed over the reins has made the Shropshire businessman a tough adversary - and lengthened the process, to the frustration of Town fans. In a club statement, Wycherley said his ownership tenure had been "an honour and a privilege" but admitted the club "needed new investment". Shrewsbury take step closer to takeover deal Shrewsbury chairman's succession plan We took our time, says Shrewsbury Town owner Wycherley After suffering relegation in his first season, Shrewsbury have since been relegated three more times - and promoted three times - in Wycherley's period as owner. But the biggest legacy of his three decades at the helm was the Town's move in 2007 from their old Gay Meadow home to a new 10,000 all-seater stadium. The first of those three promotions was under Graham Turner, who returned to the club to recreate the success they had in the late 1970s and early 1980s, taking them up in 2012. "Roland has put an awful lot into the football club," Turner told BBC Radio Shropshire. "He's kept it going, when at times it's been hard. "I've nothing but admiration for him. Over the years he's done a very good job." Wycherley's last game watching the club while at the helm was Saturday's 2-1 FA Cup first-round win at non-league Eastleigh. top.description: Nov 7, 2026; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; New York Knicks center Andre Drummond (0) stands on the court in the second quarter against the Cleveland Cavaliers at Rocket Arena. Mandatory Credit: David Richard-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Andre Drummond did not score against Cleveland, and the Knicks still got valuable minutes from their backup center. That matters for a team trying to keep its starters effective across a long season. In 14 minutes of Saturday’s 109-97 win, Drummond collected eight rebounds, including two offensive boards, with two steals and a block. New York outscored Cleveland by 10 while he was on the floor, according to the NBA box score . The value came from ending possessions, giving New York another chance on the glass and covering a stretch without asking Karl-Anthony Towns to play the entire game. I would keep a defined rebounding role for Drummond against bigger second units, especially on nights when Towns needs a breather. Extra possessions are useful, and a reserve center does not need a high usage rate to justify his minutes. 0 What do you think? Post a comment. The tradeoff is spacing. A Towns-led lineup can pull a center away from the basket in a way a traditional reserve lineup may not. Coaches can also use smaller groups against opponents who spread the floor and force repeated defensive rotations. Single-game plus-minus is noisy and does not prove Drummond alone caused the margin. The eight rebounds and the team’s ability to survive those minutes are a more useful starting point for deciding where his role fits. top.title: Yankees face a closer choice with a $23 million deadline
top.description: Oct 7, 2026; Bronx, New York, USA; New York Yankees pitcher David Bednar (53) throws during the ninth inning against the Tampa Bay Rays in game three of the ALDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Yankee Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Yankees should not assume David Bednar’s future will take care of itself while other closers come off the board. His decision on a $23.15 million qualifying offer is approaching, and the alternative could cost New York something entirely different: young talent. Milwaukee closer Trevor Megill has entered the trade discussion. Pinstripes Nation’s Sara Molnick relayed Joel Sherman’s assessment that the Brewers could explore his market. The assessment does not report that New York is currently negotiating a deal. Oct 5, 2026; St. Petersburg, Florida, USA; New York Yankees pitcher David Bednar (53) delivers a pitch during the eighth inning against the Tampa Bay Rays in game two of the ALDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Tropicana Field. Mandatory Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Yankees need more than one bullpen plan Bednar converted 35 saves with a 2.47 ERA over 69 1/3 innings in 2026. New York extended the qualifying offer, which he must accept or reject by November 17; a rejection would not prevent the sides from negotiating a longer deal. Megill saved 30 games for Milwaukee and recorded the final six outs of its championship-clinching World Series win. A trade could provide late-inning experience, but any prospect cost would come on top of his salary and the risk attached to acquiring a reliever. I would keep talking to Bednar and ask Milwaukee about Megill’s price without treating either pitcher as a guaranteed solution. Re-signing Bednar preserves prospects; acquiring Megill could leave more flexibility on the contract side, depending on the actual terms. 0 What do you think? Post a comment. Neither choice fills every opening. Paul Blackburn and several other Yankees relievers also reached free agency, so paying for a closer cannot be the entire winter plan. No public asking price or current Yankees offer is established, and Bednar may accept the one-year deal before a trade becomes necessary. top.title: PFIPC Scandal: FG Files Fresh Amended Charges Against Adeyemi Adeniyi, Four Others
top.description: The Federal Government has filed a fresh 36-count amended charge against the embattled Director-General of the Presidential Foreign Investment Promotion Council (PFIPC), Adeyemi Adeniyi, and four others over alleged forgery, false representation and fraud. Adeniyi appeared alongside his co-defendants before Justice Halilu Yusuf of the Federal Capital Territory High Court in Maitama, Abuja, on Monday. However, their arraignment on the fresh charges could not proceed due to the absence of the fourth defendant, Florence Omemah, who was reportedly ill. Prosecution counsel, Sylvanus Tahir, informed the court that Ms Omemah was receiving treatment at a hospital in Abuja. He subsequently requested a seven-day adjournment to enable her to recover and appear in court to take her plea. Counsel to Mr Adeniyi, Ibrahim Angulu, however, urged the court to grant a shorter adjournment to allow him to pursue bail for his client. He also told the court that Mr Adeniyi had been in detention for more than 200 days. In a brief ruling, Justice Yusuf adjourned the case until November 18 for the arraignment of all the defendants. The judge further ordered that Mr Adeniyi be remanded at the Kuje Correctional Centre, while the other defendants should remain in the custody of the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC). Alleged Fake Government Agency Adeniyi Adeyemi paraded himself as the DG of the PFIPC. Photo: X@BayoOnanuga. The case centres on allegations that Adeniyi established a fictitious federal agency known as the Presidential Foreign Investment Promotion Council and falsely presented himself as its director-general. Investigators alleged that the agency had no legal backing and that Mr Adeniyi forged appointment letters and signatures attributed to the Chief of Staff to the President to legitimise his purported position. According to investigators, he occupied offices previously used by the defunct Presidential Economic Advisory Council at the Federal Secretariat in Abuja and allegedly held unauthorised meetings with foreign diplomats. He was also accused of seeking official visa documentation for United States visas and operating 34 bank accounts. Investigators further alleged that he exploited loopholes in the civil service system to secure a proposed allocation of ₦1.302 billion for the fictitious agency in the 2026 budget. ICPC Uncovers Other Alleged Fake Agencies Following an interim report presented to President Bola Tinubu, the ICPC reportedly uncovered two other allegedly fictitious agencies linked to Mr Adeniyi: the FCT Investment Promotion Agency and the Foreign Investment Promotion Agency. top.title: Dodgers notes: Shoki Oda, Aaron Bates, MLB lockout
top.description: TAIPEI, TAIWAN - SEPTEMBER 12: Shoki Oda #11 of Team Japan interacts with Ritora Yamada #2 of Team Japan in the first inning during the BFA U18 Asian Baseball Championship Super Round game between Chinese Taipei and Japan at Taipei Dome on September 12, 2026 in Taipei, Taiwan. (Photo by Gene Wang - Capture At Media/Getty Images) | Getty Images Japanese right-hander Shoki Oda is one of the most interesting names of the offseason, as the 18-year-old right-hander is meeting with MLB teams, including the Dodgers . The lure of a larger bonus in the U.S. than what they might get in the NPB draft has led to some Japanese teenagers to jump stateside. Yuri Karasawa talked about this trend as well as Oda as a guest of Ben Lindbergh on an episode of the Effectively Wild Podcast last week . Karasawa went deeper into Oda with Jordan Shusterman and Jake Mintz on the Baseball Bar-B-Cast podcast . Eric Longenhagen at FanGraphs scouted several Japanese players available this winter , and wrote, “My sources tell me Oda is more likely to sign after the new international signing period begins in 2027 rather than try to sneak in before the end of 2026.” Aaron Bates and the Dodgers couldn’t come to an agreement on a contract extension which led to the hitting coach and the team parting ways last week after a dozen years coaching in the organization. Bates told Maddie Lee of the Los Angeles Times he was initially surprised by the split , but otherwise took the high road: “Processing it, I think that there’s always a time and a place, and I think that things run their course,” Bates said. “But I have nothing but amazing things to say about the Dodgers organization and people.” Ken Rosenthal and Evan Drellich at The Athletic spoke to several baseball agents , who are aligned with one another on at least one thing — MLB should not have a salary cap. This quote is from Rafa Nieves, agent of Teoscar Hernández and others: “The league proposals, and the way they are trying to bully the players, have united them,” Nieves said. “A year or two ago, I would have maybe answered differently. … But when you come up with these proposals, just insulting them, it is going to wrangle them together. Which is what I have noticed: They’re more united, they’re more together, they’re getting more informed.”

top.title: Blackburn Rovers 2-1 West Ham - the fans' verdict
top.description: [BBC] We asked for your thoughts after Blackburn Rovers beat West Ham 2-1 at Ewood Park in the Championship on Saturday. Here are some of your comments: Blackburn fans Keith: Typical Rovers, always play better against fancied teams but a good rehearsal for our next match against somebody else in claret and blue. One new manager bounce overcome. Let's hope for another next time out. Ronnie: West Ham thought they just had to turn up and Blackburn would roll over. Well that went well for them. Rob: A team that has more chance of going up than West Ham. They certainly had West Ham's mark. Vicky: Perfect day - Rovers win and Burnley lose from 4-1 up. Jeff: Actually inspiring from Rovers for once. Tony has done a great job so far, and a great atmosphere at the end. We turned the pressure on us in the first half to a win- so well done lads. John: I can honestly say it's the best Rovers game I've seen for a long time, they played their hearts out. As Rovers fan I couldn't be more chuffed for the way they stuck together, and showed such grit and determination. And it paid off. West Ham fans Clive: A new manager can't improve players that are not good enough to put a West Ham shirt on their backs. At least six players are not good enough to play in the Championship. West Ham will not get promotion until you change the core squad. One chance - January transfer window. Paul: Not good enough. I remember last time we went down we just managed to win promotion through the play-offs. Same thing this time, I fear. Sue: Played better but still don't take their chances. We could have won easily if they had taken their chances when they were in the box. Definitely need a centre forward. Got to keep confident and give Scott Parker a chance. He's only had four days. Ewan: West Ham were clearly not clinical in the final third, Blackburn defended brilliantly and West Ham's wingers could not get past Blackburn's full-backs. Simply not good enough from a West Ham perspective. Nigel: Hopefully reality is dawning on a squad full of ego and delusions of grandeur. They need to go back to basics, many weren't good enough for the Premier League and are now being found out in the Championship. A root and branch update is needed and Scotty should take the opportunity to ring serious changes during this international break. If we do not go up at the first time of asking I fear our stay in this division will be a prolonged one. Sofian: It was actually a decent performance compared to recent weeks. We pressed well, looked more comfortable in playing the game against a low block and we created plenty. However this defence and the goalkeeper are simply below par. Mads Hermansen needs dropping for Alphonse Areola and we need to start winning games, and quick, in order to push for an automatic promotion spot.

top.title: England call up Burn as Guéhi pulls out of squad
top.description: FILE PHOTO - England manager Thomas Tuchel reacts during a media conference at Wembley Stadium. (is associated with: «England call up Burn as Guéhi pulls out of squad») Jonathan Brady/PA Wire/dpa Thomas Tuchel has recalled Dan Burn following Marc Guéhi’s withdrawal from the squad for England’s Nations League doubleheader. Tuchel’s side round off the year with Thursday’s Wembley encounter against Croatia and a trip to world champions Spain on Sunday. Manchester City defender Guéhi has featured in England’s last 15 matches but will miss those games due to a reported hip issue, which has led to Newcastle defender Burn’s first call-up since the summer. A statement from the Football Association read: "Dan Burn has been added to the England squad following the withdrawal of Marc Guéhi through injury. "The Newcastle United defender, who has 11 caps, joined up with the rest of Thomas Tuchel’s group at Tottenham Hotspur’s training ground on Monday. Guéhi was substituted at half-time of Manchester City’s fixture at Nottingham Forest on Saturday and will now remain with his club."

nigeria.description: . Seeks media partnership to safeguard democracy . Warns against fake results, inflammatory rhetoric By Steve Oko & Chinedu Adonu The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has condemned the “rig and die” slogan being popularised by some political actors ahead of the 2027 general elections, warning that it could expose innocent Nigerians to electoral violence. The Commission also vowed that any electoral official, including ad hoc personnel, found to have compromised the electoral process would face the full weight of the law. INEC National Commissioner and Chairman, Information and Voter Education Committee, Mohammed Kudu Haruna, gave the warnings at a media engagement forum for journalists and media executives from the South-East, South-South and South-West geopolitical zones in Enugu. Haruna cautioned politicians against inflammatory rhetoric and threats capable of endangering ordinary Nigerians engaged as presiding officers, ad hoc staff, party agents and election observers. He stressed that disagreements over electoral outcomes should be resolved through lawful channels, including complaints to INEC, security agencies and the courts, rather than violence. The National Commissioner also sought stronger collaboration with the media to safeguard democracy and ensure credible, peaceful and transparent conduct of the 2027 elections. Describing the media as critical to electoral credibility, he said public confidence in the electoral process depended largely on the accuracy, fairness and professionalism of election reporting. He cautioned journalists against spreading misinformation, unverified results, manipulated videos and inflammatory political narratives capable of undermining public confidence and triggering violence. Haruna particularly warned against premature declaration of results, sensational reporting and presenting projections as official results. “Results are declared only by the Commission through its duly appointed returning officers. Projections and unofficial figures must be clearly labelled as such,” he said. He urged journalists to verify allegations against INEC through its official channels before publication and report electoral incidents with sensitivity, distinguishing between events personally witnessed and information obtained from other sources. The National Commissioner further called for inclusive election reporting that gives adequate attention to women, youths and persons with disabilities, particularly the challenges they face in participating in the electoral process. He urged media organisations to intensify voter education, especially on Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs), accreditation procedures, electronic transmission of results and peaceful participation. nigeria.title: CHOGM 2026: Bianca seeks stronger commonwealth cooperation
nigeria.description: Nigeria has called for stronger cooperation among Commonwealth member states to address security challenges, expand trade, strengthen democratic institutions and promote climate resilience. The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu, disclosed this on Monday in a post on her X account, detailing Nigeria’s expectations from the Commonwealth following her interventions at the 2026 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) in Antigua. She said Nigeria emphasised the need for collective action on peace and security, trade, climate resilience and youth empowerment, particularly in combating terrorism and expanding access to development finance. Odumegwu-Ojukwu also drew attention to Nigeria’s preparations for the 2027 general elections, stressing the importance of supporting free, fair and credible electoral processes through election monitoring groups and stronger democratic institutions across member states. According to her, Nigeria, under President Bola Tinubu’s leadership, remains committed to promoting democracy, consensus, civil, political and social rights, while upholding the rule of law and judicial independence. She described the creation of the Commonwealth Trade Portal as a welcome development, noting that trade facilitation initiatives would promote economic growth, strengthen trade links among member states and help developing economies integrate into the global financial market. The minister further urged the Commonwealth to give greater attention to women and girls affected by conflicts, displacement and climate change. She said their access to essential services, livelihood opportunities and justice should remain central to collective responses, adding that their voices must shape solutions to the challenges they face. On reparatory justice, Odumegwu-Ojukwu identified the agenda as a major highlight of the ministerial meeting, particularly the agreement by the United Kingdom government to engage in structured, time-bound, inclusive and good-faith dialogue with affected countries over the transatlantic trafficking of enslaved Africans and its historical consequences. She said Nigeria hoped that the commitments adopted at CHOGM 2026 would translate into practical actions capable of creating jobs, strengthening security and improving the lives of citizens across Commonwealth member states. nigeria.title: Musiala’s condition cannot be cured, may never return to best — Bayern president
nigeria.description: Bayern Munich honorary president Uli Hoeness has raised concerns over Jamal Musiala’s long-term future, saying the Germany international is suffering from a condition that cannot be permanently cured and may never regain his previous level of performance. According to BBC Sport, Hoeness said the 23-year-old forward’s condition could only be managed to some extent with medication, leaving the club uncertain about whether he would return to his best. “We are facing a dilemma in this case, as he is suffering from an illness that cannot simply be cured, but it can be controlled to a certain extent with the use of medication,” Hoeness told Bavarian broadcaster BR24. He also questioned whether Musiala would ever recover the level he displayed before his health problems, while acknowledging that Bayern would continue to support the player, who is under contract until 2030. “But the question remains: will he one day be able to regain the level he used to show?” Hoeness said. Hoeness further suggested that the situation had created a contractual dilemma for the German champions, claiming Musiala’s condition was not covered by the insurance attached to his deal. “Imagine if Bayern Munich now decided to question his contract, and told him: what you are able to offer currently no longer matches the level stipulated in the contract,” he said. Musiala’s health concerns emerged during pre-season after he collapsed twice within four days. He was subsequently reported to have a treatable neurological dysfunction. The forward has also been sidelined by a hamstring injury sustained in September and has yet to feature for Bayern since then, although he has recently returned to training. He has scored twice in four appearances for the German champions in all competitions this season. Former Bayern and Germany captain Lothar Matthaus, however, interpreted Hoeness’ comments as an attempt to challenge and motivate the youngster rather than write him off. “He’s needling him a little. It’s not just about wrapping him in cotton wool. He also has to battle against adversity sometimes,” Matthaus told Sky90. Matthaus added that Hoeness wanted Musiala to respond to the remarks by proving he could return to his previous level. “Uli was looking to create that adversity with this statement. “It’s fine for him to say something like that, because we can’t just put a positive spin on things and somehow wait for him to come back. “If I were in Jamal Musiala’s position, that would be motivation enough to show Uli I’m back.” Musiala joined Bayern in 2019 after coming through Chelsea’s academy and has since scored 71 goals and provided 38 assists in 235 appearances for the club. He has earned 46 caps for Germany and shared the Golden Boot as joint-top scorer at Euro 2024. nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, has announced the restoration of electricity to several areas affected by recent power disruptions in Lagos, Ogun, Oyo, Kwara and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), assuring Nigerians that the government is working to provide reliable electricity and sustain grid stability. Tegbe disclosed this in an update shared on his Facebook page on Monday, saying efforts were continuing to restore full electricity supply to the remaining affected locations. He said the vandalised Benin-Egbin 330kV transmission line had been repaired and returned to service, helping to increase power supply to the Lagos Complex to more than 1,000 megawatts. “This restoration helped to bring the total power supply to the Lagos Complex to over 1,000 megawatts, effectively normalising to the condition before the disruption,” he said. “We are working with the key power sector stakeholders, including the Generation Companies, System Operator, Transmission Company and the Distribution Companies to ensure sustained and improved availability of power,” he said. The minister assured consumers that efforts were continuing to restore electricity to the remaining affected areas. “Our teams continue to work to restore full supply to the remaining affected locations,” he said. Tegbe reiterated the government’s commitment to improving electricity supply across the country, saying reliable power remained the ministry’s priority. “Our priority continues to be the provision of reliable electricity to Nigerians,” he added. The development follows widespread power disruptions across parts of the country, with electricity allocation to distribution companies reportedly falling to about 2,926 megawatts on November 5. The Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) attributed the decline to inadequate gas supply to thermal power plants and reduced output from hydroelectric stations, which contributed to shorter hours of electricity supply and increased load shedding. nigeria.title: UK moves to end early GCSE teaching in Year 7–9 shake-up
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The UK government plans to stop secondary schools from routinely teaching the General Certificate of Secondary Education (GCSE) content before Year 10, as part of a curriculum overhaul aimed at making the first three years of secondary school more engaging. According to BBC News, the Department for Education (DfE) says it wants to restore Key Stage 3 (Years 7 to 9) as a distinct phase, giving pupils more time to build their knowledge and explore a broader range of subjects before beginning GCSE courses. The plan follows concerns that early exam preparation is narrowing what pupils learn. A survey cited by the government found that more than half of teachers said GCSE courses were dominating the first three years of secondary school, even though GCSE content is intended to begin in Year 10. Education Secretary Lucy Powell said some pupils were being rushed towards exams before they had grasped the fundamentals. She said the government would protect time in Years 7 to 9 for deeper learning and a wider curriculum. The proposed changes would also make room for subjects including drama, physical education, music and modern foreign languages, alongside technical and digital skills. The DfE says the curriculum will place greater emphasis on confident speaking, reading and numeracy. The government says persistent absence nearly doubles between Year 7 and Year 9, reaching one in four pupils. It hopes a more engaging curriculum will help address disengagement and improve attendance and outcomes. Schools would still be able to stretch pupils who are ready to progress further, while avoiding routinely narrowing subject choices or requiring large groups to start GCSE specifications early. The full curriculum is expected to be published later this year as the announcement concerns England’s education system. nigeria.title: Independent Russian Novaya Gazeta newspaper shuts down
nigeria.description: Russia’s flagship independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta on Monday held its final editorial meeting and emptied its office after it said last month it was closing under the Kremlin’s pressure. Novaya Gazeta was for years one of the last outlets to openly criticise the authorities and Moscow’s Ukraine war amid a tightening grip on free speech and a campaign against dissent. It was branded a “foreign agent” – a label reminiscent of Soviet-era repression – and saw its journalists detained and questioned. On Monday, Novaya Gazeta held its last editorial meeting, the Russian Sota Vision and Ostorozhno Novosti outlets reported. Images published by Ostorozhno Novosti showed the paper’s editor-in-chief, Sergei Sokolov, taking down photographs of its reporters murdered in killings widely seen as retribution for their work. They included a picture of Anna Politkovskaya, who spent years investigating allegations of abuses by Russia’s military during its campaigns in Chechnya and was an early critic of President Vladimir Putin’s long rule. She was found dead in her apartment block on Putin’s birthday in October 2006. In an emotional video last month, Sokolov said the paper had “been killed” and was shutting down after “the Russian authorities — the Russian special services – have forced the editorial team to end its work”. Rights groups including Reporters Without Borders and Amnesty International condemned the move. The newspaper’s closure was “yet another devastating blow for remaining independent media in the Russian Federation” UN rights chief Volker Turk said in a statement in October. But Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov on Monday called it “a normal cycle of change”. “It would be wrong to say that the era of independent Russian media is coming to an end. The Russian media is highly diverse and is developing in a highly competitive environment,” Peskov told reporters. Moscow has introduced unprecedented censorship while troops fight in Ukraine, forcing most independent media into exile. Founded in 1993 after the collapse of the Soviet Union, Novaya Gazeta was one of Russia’s most reputable and renowned organisations reporting and documenting human rights abuses. nigeria.title: 375 judges sworn in for 2027 election tribunals
nigeria.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri, Abuja With 68 days to the 2027 general elections, 375 judges were inaugurated on Monday to serve on tribunals that will hear election petitions filed by aggrieved parties across the country. Also Read: * How do election petitions work in Nigeria? * What is 25% requirement in Nigeria’s presidential election? Section 285(1) and (2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, vests in the President of the Court of Appeal the responsibility of constituting Election Petition Tribunals for the adjudication of disputes arising from National and State Houses of Assembly and Governorship elections. Similarly, Section 134(3)(a) and (b) of the Electoral Act, 2026, prescribes the timelines for constituting the tribunals and opening their registries. In her address at the occasion held at the Body of Benchers Complex in Abuja, the President of the Court of Appeal, Justice Monica Dongban-Mensem, said the inauguration of the tribunal judges highlighted a collective commitment to constitutional democracy, the rule of law, and the integrity of Nigeria’s electoral process. “This gathering is more than a ceremonial event; it is an important institutional preparation for one of the most consequential responsibilities entrusted to the judiciary. “The credibility of democracy depends not only on the conduct of elections but also on the existence of impartial, effective, and timely mechanisms for resolving electoral disputes. “Through the fair determination of such disputes, the Judiciary safeguards the people’s mandate, upholds constitutional supremacy and sustains public confidence in democratic governance,” the Court of Appeal President added. She urged the judges to be mindful that the judiciary will be subject to considerable public scrutiny owing to their actions. Justice Dongban-Mensem disclosed that the 375 tribunal judges were nominated from various courts and judicial institutions across the country. “Of this number, 138 are returning members with previous Tribunal experience, while 237 are newly nominated members,” she added. Oduntan also criticised what he described as a return to the blame game among operators in the electricity sector, recalling that similar disagreements between stakeholders had characterised the industry between 2016 and 2019. He said distribution companies, transmission operators, generation companies and gas suppliers had previously blamed one another for poor electricity supply instead of addressing the underlying problems. “Our major problem is that we have started that very wrong route that we went through between 2016 and 2019. What is that? nigeria.title: Troops kill suspect, recover AK-47 in old Oyo park
nigeria.description: By: Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Operation IGBO DANU II, under the 2 Division of the Nigerian Army, have neutralised a suspected criminal and recovered an AK-47 rifle and other weapons during an operation in the Old Oyo National Park. The operation, conducted in collaboration with hybrid forces, also led to the destruction of temporary shelters suspected to have been used as hideouts by criminal elements operating in the forest. The Nigerian Army disclosed this in a statement, saying the encounter occurred on November 7, 2026, when troops conducting operations within the park engaged suspected criminals who fled upon sighting the advancing forces. The statement said the troops subsequently recovered an AK-47 rifle, one empty magazine and a Dane gun from the area. It added that during a follow-up operation on November 8, troops discovered the corpse of one of the fleeing suspects, confirming that one criminal element had been neutralised. According to the Army, the destruction of the temporary shelters was aimed at disrupting criminal activities and denying the suspects safe havens within the forested area. It said troops, in collaboration with other security stakeholders, remained committed to sustaining operations to dismantle criminal networks, deny them operational bases and restore security across the 2 Division Area of Responsibility. nigeria.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe, Umuahia Abia State Governor, Dr Alex Chioma Otti, has said that the achievements recorded by his administration in the last three years represent only the foundation of his development agenda, assuring that the next four and a half years will focus on consolidating the gains and entrenching reforms across the state. Otti, who stated this during the South-East Conference of Dominion City Global, held in Aba, assured residents that his administration is committed to taking the state to the next level of development. Describing the achievements of his administration as a dress rehearsal, Otti said his government is determined to deepen ongoing reforms and deliver practical development outcomes that would have a lasting impact on the lives of the people. He said, “What has happened here is what I call a dress rehearsal, to let people know that they haven’t seen anything yet. What we have built in the last three years is just the foundation. “So, the next four and a half years, we will use them to consolidate. And when I say consolidation, I mean consolidation – changes that are irreversible. “My administration is not interested in making unrealistic promises but in implementing practical policies and projects capable of transforming the state.” He disclosed that his government is working towards ensuring a constant electricity supply across the state. According to him, the move would enable Abia to strengthen its electricity regulatory framework, support power generation and distribution capacity, and facilitate the distribution of excess electricity to other parts of the state. The governor also noted that his administration had instituted a monthly media chat to ensure that residents are adequately informed about government activities, policies and achievements. Otti reiterated his administration’s commitment to fairness, equity and merit in governance, declaring that there is no state-of-origin discrimination in Abia, as everyone living in the state is regarded as an Abian and treated equally. He charged Christians to demonstrate their faith through practical actions, adding that meaningful progress requires commitment, hard work and personal responsibility, as people should not expect miracles without making the necessary efforts. The governor congratulated the leadership of Dominion City Global on the conference and the construction of its massive facility in Aba, expressing admiration for the scale of the project and commending the church for its commitment to advancing the work of God. The State Commissioner for Information, Culture and Tourism, Dr. Nawani Aboki, gave the assurance while addressing journalists, stakeholders, party supporters and government partners in Lafia on Monday. Aboki said the government was monitoring the security situation across the state’s local government areas to ensure that voters could exercise their franchise without fear or intimidation. Warning those contemplating violence, the commissioner said the government’s preference for peace should not be mistaken for weakness. “Quietness does not mean that somebody is weak. At times, when someone is pushed, the time comes when they must act. “Anyone who wants to perpetuate violence will be arrested and prosecuted to ensure we have peaceful elections,” he warned. He urged political parties and candidates to conduct their campaigns in an orderly and civilised manner, stressing that political violence would serve no useful purpose in the electoral process or the development of the state. Buni spoke on Sunday night in Abuja at the Yobe Development and Partnership Roundtable, where he engaged distinguished indigenes of the state residing outside the state. He said the improved security situation had enabled farmers to return to their farmlands, while business owners could move freely across communities to conduct legitimate commercial activities. “Yobe State today enjoys relative peace across the 17 local government areas. Our farmers in the last few years have had access to their farmlands, while businessmen and women continue to traverse the length and breadth of the state conducting legitimate businesses peacefully,” the governor said. Recalling the difficult period of insurgency, Buni said the state had suffered widespread killings, displacement, destruction of communities and loss of livelihoods. “A few years back, our story was different, pathetic and despicable. entertainment.title: Israel Olaleye: What Selling Land Taught Me About How Nigerians Think About Money
entertainment.description: In 2021, I graduated from the University of Ibadan with a degree in Mathematics. I thought my life would be about numbers on a whiteboard. I did not know it would become about numbers in people’s bank accounts, and the fears, hopes and contradictions that sit behind them. By mid-2023, I had taken a job selling real estate. I started at the very bottom, as a sales development representative: the person who makes the first call, sends the message and follows up when nobody replies. Today, I manage a sales team. Somewhere between then and now, I stopped seeing real estate as a business of land and buildings. I started seeing it as a mirror. Put a property in front of a Nigerian, and you will learn, very quickly, how they think about money. Here is some of what that mirror has shown me: A prospect once told me, with complete confidence, “I have my money ready for the land.” We fixed an inspection. We walked the site together under the afternoon sun, red earth on our shoes. Then, standing on the plot, the prospect asked if they could pay next year. I was not angry. I understood. Saying “I am ready” feels good. Being ready is different. It means you have decided what the money is for, and you are willing to let it go. I have seen versions of that moment many times. The client who books an inspection for 2 pm and is still not there at 4 pm. The person who asks for options, receives ten properties that match exactly what they requested, and replies, “Do you have something else?” The buyer who is ready until it is time to decide, and then needs three more months to think. The one who disappeared after asking for a price came back after the price went up, and asked for the old price. For a long time, these moments frustrated me. But they taught me that most people do not have a money problem. They have a decision problem. We are a generation that earns, spends, plans and postpones, often all at the same time. You can earn a lot and still not be wealthy One idea I keep returning to is that you can earn twenty million naira a year and still not be wealthy. Income is what comes in. Wealth is what stays and grows. Two people can earn the same salary and end up in completely different places ten years later, simply because one converted part of that income into assets and the other converted all of it into lifestyle. Wealthy people do not always look wealthy. Some of the most financially secure people I have met do not drive the loudest cars. entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky , her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis . The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. SHOW AND AVAILABILITY Earth & Sky will be presented on November 11, 2026, and will be available from December 2026 at the Banke Kuku flagship on Victoria Island, Lagos, and through global stockists. entertainment.description: Over 10,000 women gathered at the Landmark Event Centre, Victoria Island, Lagos, on October 31, 2026, for the fourth edition of FinTribe Finance Fair , a growing movement dedicated to helping African women move from financial awareness to wealth creation and ownership. Themed I CAN and powered by returning lead sponsor Sycamore, the event brought together financial experts, business leaders, entrepreneurs and influential personalities, including Funke Akindele , Omoni Oboli , BamBam , Sola Adesakin and Olufemi Shobanjo , for a day of practical financial education, inspiring conversations and meaningful opportunities. For FinTribe founder Jennifer Awirigwe , popularly known as Financial Jennifer, the fair represents a bigger mission: helping women gain the confidence and resources to take charge of their financial futures. “Financial education is important, but knowledge must eventually become action. We want women to leave Finance Fair knowing that they can save, invest, grow their income, build businesses and take ownership of their financial future,” she shared ahead of the event. Beyond Finance Fair, FinTribe is building a community where women learn about money and put that knowledge into practice . With a presence across 43 countries, the organisation has reached over 20,000 women through financial education, supported more than 5,000 women with capital market training and helped members collectively save and invest millions of dollars. Through its Wealth Builders Academy, savings and investment community, real estate initiatives and recently launched FinTribe App, the organisation continues to create opportunities for women to build healthier financial habits, develop investment confidence and work towards long-term financial independence. At the fair, award-winning filmmaker Omoni Oboli encouraged women to pursue their ambitions without neglecting their wellbeing, reminding them to take things one step at a time, prioritise rest and ask for help when needed. During the Financial Clinic, Sola Adesakin challenged women to become more intentional about their finances, emphasising the importance of earning, budgeting and turning income into real assets. She also introduced the four forces of money: Earnings, Expenses, Engines and Encumbrances. Olufemi Shobanjo of NGX Regulation Limited shared insights into capital market participation, while actress BamBam, marketing strategist and Woof Studios founder Adetutu Laditan, and Mercy Agbeti, popularly known as Christian Money Woman, contributed to conversations about building value, navigating opportunities and growing with purpose. entertainment.title: Inside the Story of Martell’s Afrobeats Limited Edition XO with Davido and Prince Gyasi
entertainment.description: There’s something special about a collaboration that brings together music and visual art, particularly when both creatives have spent years helping African culture reach audiences around the world. For its latest limited edition, Maison Martell has brought together Nigerian music superstar Davido and Ghanaian visual artist Prince Gyasi to create a new expression of its prestigious XO cognac , inspired by the sound, movement and global influence of Afrobeats. The Martell Afrobeats Limited Edition XO will be unveiled in Nigeria on November 6, following the collection’s global launch in New York on October 28. At the heart of the collaboration is Prince Gyasi’s distinctive artistic language. Known for his vibrant colours and imaginative compositions, Gyasi has created an original artwork of Davido that features on the limited-edition bottle and presentation box. The design draws inspiration from the landscapes of West Africa, bringing together Martell’s iconic blue with shades of amber and gold. The blue reflects the rhythmic flow of the ocean, while the golden tones evoke sunlit sands and the warmth of African sunsets. Reimagined through Gyasi’s distinctive, hyper-surreal visual style, these elements create a composition that captures the movement and energy of Afrobeats while celebrating the unity, strength and creative spirit of the continent. For Gyasi, the inspiration goes beyond the visual appeal of the bottle. Growing up in Ghana, his experience of music and its ability to bring people together informed the creative direction of the collaboration. “Growing up in Ghana, I’ve seen firsthand how music brings people together, sparking connection, celebration, and pure joy. As Davido says, ‘We rise by lifting others,’ a reminder that music builds community and lifts us all. I feel a deep pride in Afrobeats, its incredible journey, and the mark it’s making on global music,” Prince Gyasi said. He further explained the thinking behind the colours and composition: “Inspired by the landscapes of West Africa, I blended Martell’s iconic blue with the rhythmic flow of the ocean, golden sands, and waves reimagined in a hyper-surreal style, bringing sound and movement to life. Shades of amber and gold capture the warmth of African sunsets and speak to the continent’s unity, strength, and deep spirit.” The result is an artwork that positions the limited-edition XO as more than a presentation of the cognac itself. It offers a visual interpretation of Afrobeats and recognises the artists and communities whose creativity has helped the genre travel across borders and influence audiences globally. The project also reflects Martell’s five-year relationship with Davido, whose career has developed alongside the international growth of Afrobeats. Bringing Prince Gyasi into the collaboration introduces another creative perspective, connecting music and contemporary African art through a shared celebration of African expression. entertainment.title: UK-based OBIMI Brings Families Together in Lagos to Support Children With Disabilities
entertainment.description: OBIMI CIC is a UK-based community organisation supporting parents and caregivers of children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). Its founder, Helen Ewumi , is a qualified social worker and a parent of children with disabilities. Her professional experience and family life both inform OBIMI’s commitment to helping families feel heard, supported and less alone. The Nigeria outreach brought families together in Lagos to share experiences and raise awareness about the importance of understanding disability and challenging stigma. Around 100 families received support through the outreach, including food hampers. Clothing was also shared with families. During the visit, the OBIMI team went to a special school in Lagos and gave pupils school bags and stationery. These practical gifts were offered to support children with their learning and to remind them that they are valued and included. The gathering also created space for families to connect and take part in conversations about disability. OBIMI’s message was clear: every child deserves to belong, and families should be met with understanding, respect and support. For Helen, taking OBIMI’s work to Nigeria was an opportunity to connect with families and communities in Lagos. As a social worker and a parent with lived experience of caring for children with disabilities, she understands how important it is for families to feel listened to and supported. OBIMI CIC is grateful to the families, school staff, volunteers, partners and supporters who helped make the outreach possible. The organisation hopes to continue building connections and raising awareness so that children with disabilities and their families can feel seen, supported and included. A UK-based social worker and parent of children with disabilities, Helen founded OBIMI to support families and challenge disability stigma. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. Loving Itohan is in cinemas nationwide from 6 November 2026. entertainment.title: Africa Comedy Live Brings Its Platform to Africa, Opening With an Invitation-Only Founding Gathering in Lagos
entertainment.description: Africa Comedy Live (ACL), the platform connecting African comedians, content creators and audiences across the continent and the diaspora, today announces its arrival in Africa with an invitation-only founding gathering, A Salute to Nollywood, to be held on Friday, 13 November 2026 at TRIB3 , Victoria Island, Lagos. The evening marks two milestones at once: the introduction of the Africa Comedy Live platform to the African market, and a formal salute to the comedians and storytellers whose work built the audience that African comedy now commands. Africa Comedy Live has been presenting African comedy live in the United States since 2019, with artists including Kenny Blaq , Helen Paul , Real Warri Pikin and David Operah . The platform, live at www.africacomedylive.com, is another channel, not a replacement for the ones creators already use. It allows creators to keep the audiences they have already built, earn more, and expand opportunities across continents, while giving viewers across Africa and the diaspora a single place to discover the comedians and creators worth following. A Salute to Nollywood brings together comedians, entertainment professionals, media and prospective partners for an evening built around three things: an introduction to the platform through a live demonstration, a celebration of African comedy, and a salute to the generation of performers whose influence continues to shape new talent. “Africa’s comedy has never lacked talent. What it has lacked is a stage that belongs to it,” said Carrie Crawford, Founder of Africa Comedy Live. “For seven years we have put African comedians in front of live audiences in the United States. Now we are bringing that home. Africa Comedy Live is that permanent stage, and Lagos is where it begins,” He added. The gathering is by invitation only and is not open to public attendance. For comedy lovers, the evening is an introduction to the platform and a way to follow the journey. For creators, it is an opportunity to express interest in joining the community. For brands and partners, it is a chance to explore ways to support African comedy’s next chapter. ABOUT AFRICA COMEDY LIVE Africa Comedy Live is a web platform connecting African comedians, content creators and brands across the continent and the diaspora. Founded by Carrie Crawford, ACL has presented African comedy live in the United States since 2019 and is built on a simple conviction: Africa’s comedy deserves a world stage, and a place to call home. sports.description: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images Tim Parker played his last professional game on Saturday, November 7, 2026. The 33-year-old defender stepped onto the field at Sports Illustrated Stadium in Harrison, New Jersey, for one final match. He came on in the 90th minute to replace Sekou Kone during a 3-0 victory over Atlanta United. The crowd watched a local boy finish his career with a win, playing into the third minute of stoppage time before the final whistle blew. This was not just a game; it was the end of a 12-year journey through Major League Soccer. Parker, a native of Hicksville, New York, played 304 league matches in total. He chose to leave the sport on his own terms after a decade of hard work. The Red Bull New York team honored him by handing him the captain’s armband for this farewell performance. A Career Built on Hard Work Parker’s path to the top was not easy. He spent five years with Vancouver, making 100 appearances and scoring four goals. In 2015, he helped his team win the Canadian Championship. His time in Houston came next, where he played for two seasons and served as co-captain for both 2021 and 2022. He also spent two seasons with St. Louis CITY SC, scoring six goals there, including the very first goal in the club’s history. His most successful stretch came with the Red Bulls, where he played five seasons and made 128 appearances across all competitions. This number is higher than his time with any other club. In his first year with New York in 2018, he helped the team win the Supporters Shield. That same year, the club set a record for the most points in a single MLS season. The defense Parker anchored allowed only 33 goals, which was the fewest in the league. They also kept 15 clean sheets, the highest total in the league that year. Leadership That Went Beyond the Field Head coach Michael Bradley spoke highly of Parker’s character after the match. Bradley noted that the veteran’s career speaks for itself. He said, “Tim’s career speaks for itself.” The coach emphasized that Parker gave every team he joined leadership, presence, and quality. Bradley explained that the way Parker treated his teammates made him a proud figure in the dressing room. Julian de Guzman, the Head of Sport for Red Bull New York, also praised the retiring defender. According to reports, he has maintained an outstanding professional status throughout his career. De Guzman noted that Parker earned the respect of everyone he played with and worked alongside. At every club he represented, Parker’s leadership, professionalism, commitment, and passion made him an important figure, he highlighted. The official statement from the club confirmed that Parker’s impact extends well beyond what he accomplished on the field. According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , the Jaguars are sending the Atlanta Falcons two draft picks to acquire Pro Bowl safety Jessie Bates, one of the best safeties in the NFL, to get a major upgrade on the defensive side of the ball. Jaguars to acquire Jessie Bates from Falcons for two picks "Trade: Falcons are sending former Pro Bowl safety Jessie Bates to the Jacksonville Jaguars in exchange for a 2027 2nd-round pick and a 2028 5th-round pick, sources tell ESPN," Schefter reports. This is a massive move for the Jaguars prior to the Tuesday trade deadline, as Bates is one of the best defensive backs in the NFL and was one of the more intriguing trade candidates seemingly available this season. He's a 29-year-old safety who was a Pro Bowler one time back in 2023. While he might not have a lot of accolades, Bates is an incredible DB who will be a major upgrade in Jacksonville. MORE : 4 stats that show how bad Chargers' Justin Herbert has been in 2026 In his nine-year NFL career, Bates has 28 interceptions, four pick-sixes, 74 passes defended, 14 forced fumbles, 871 tackles, and one sack. This season for the Falcons, Bates has 60 total tackles with one fumble returned for a touchdown, three forced fumbles, one interception, and three passes defended. There might not have been a better safety on the trade block this season than Bates, and James Gladstone is swinging big with this major acquisition. It's a big trade, as the Jaguars giving up a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick isn't a cheap package to give up for a rental DB. But with a real chance of winning the Super Bowl, the Jaguars are going all in. sports.title: Friedel group completes Shrewsbury Town takeover
sports.description: Roland Wycherley has been Shrewsbury Town owner and chairman since 1996 [Shrewsbury Town FC] Shrewsbury Town's long-drawn-out takeover deal has been completed, allowing former USA international goalkeeper Brad Friedel to come in as the Shropshire outfit's new sporting director. The paperwork on the share purchase agreement with Scott Davidson's American-based consortium Biscayne ST LLC - which includes Friedel - has been finalised, taking up 87.4 per cent of the League Two club's shares and allowing long-time owner Roland Wycherley to finally let go. Miami-based businessman Davidson is joined on the new Town board by New York financier Will Dotson and Craig Graham, chairman of Spartans, the Edinburgh-based Scottish League Two club, while former Liverpool, Blackburn Rovers, Aston Villa and Tottenham Hotspur keeper Friedel will come in to take a hands-on role, working with manager Gavin Cowan. Davidson becomes chairman of the board, which still includes existing members Liam Dooley, the club's chief executive, and Duncan Montgomery, while another ex-goalkeeper, Bryan Finnerty, is to join the group, pending the EFL's owners and directors' tests. After 30 years of leading the Shropshire club, since succeeding Ray Bailey as chairman in the summer of 1996, Wycherley can now retire at the age of 85. The Shrewsbury-born lifelong fan first made his intention clear to sell more than five years ago when the Town were still a League One club. But his dogged determination to do a deal he had to be convinced was right for the club's long-term future before he handed over the reins has made the Shropshire businessman a tough adversary - and lengthened the process, to the frustration of Town fans. In a club statement, Wycherley said his ownership tenure had been "an honour and a privilege" but admitted the club "needed new investment". Shrewsbury take step closer to takeover deal Shrewsbury chairman's succession plan We took our time, says Shrewsbury Town owner Wycherley After suffering relegation in his first season, Shrewsbury have since been relegated three more times - and promoted three times - in Wycherley's period as owner. But the biggest legacy of his three decades at the helm was the Town's move in 2007 from their old Gay Meadow home to a new 10,000 all-seater stadium. The first of those three promotions was under Graham Turner, who returned to the club to recreate the success they had in the late 1970s and early 1980s, taking them up in 2012. "Roland has put an awful lot into the football club," Turner told BBC Radio Shropshire. "He's kept it going, when at times it's been hard. "I've nothing but admiration for him. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Yankees should not assume David Bednar’s future will take care of itself while other closers come off the board. His decision on a $23.15 million qualifying offer is approaching, and the alternative could cost New York something entirely different: young talent. Milwaukee closer Trevor Megill has entered the trade discussion. Pinstripes Nation’s Sara Molnick relayed Joel Sherman’s assessment that the Brewers could explore his market. The assessment does not report that New York is currently negotiating a deal. Oct 5, 2026; St. Petersburg, Florida, USA; New York Yankees pitcher David Bednar (53) delivers a pitch during the eighth inning against the Tampa Bay Rays in game two of the ALDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Tropicana Field. Megill saved 30 games for Milwaukee and recorded the final six outs of its championship-clinching World Series win. A trade could provide late-inning experience, but any prospect cost would come on top of his salary and the risk attached to acquiring a reliever. I would keep talking to Bednar and ask Milwaukee about Megill’s price without treating either pitcher as a guaranteed solution. Re-signing Bednar preserves prospects; acquiring Megill could leave more flexibility on the contract side, depending on the actual terms. 0 What do you think? Post a comment. No public asking price or current Yankees offer is established, and Bednar may accept the one-year deal before a trade becomes necessary.
